detail.title: Operational Criteria for Objective Records
detail.summary: Objective records arise when an environment redundantly encodes and broadcasts pointer states of a system (Quantum Darwinism), providing multiple observers access to the same information. Crucially, environmental redundancy alone is insufficient; effective accessibility is gated by observer-dependent thresholds.
detail.reason: Synthesizing evidence regarding objectivity and redundancy.

detail.title: Robustness of Physical Records
detail.summary: Robustness occurs when multiple independent observers arrive at consistent records of system states. This consistency is secured by the stability of einselected states which minimize decoherence and environmental noise.

detail.title: Information Scrambling and Record Accessibility
detail.summary: Quantum scrambling delocalizes information, complicating local retrieval. However, effective records remain accessible if the scrambling process respects specific pointer states that remain detectable despite global delocalization.

detail.title: Information Scrambling and Record Accessibility
detail.summary: Quantum scrambling delocalizes information, but local observer accessibility can be evaluated via operator purity, entanglement measures, and noisy-threshold aperture functions.
detail.reason: Revise notebook nb-scrambling-records-01 with new evidence supporting scrambling and accessibility.

detail.title: Information Scrambling and Record Accessibility
detail.summary: Quantum scrambling delocalizes information across many degrees of freedom, but observer access can still be evaluated via operator purity, entanglement measures, and noisy threshold functions.
